description: Jupyter Book framework layer — seeds content/chapter-1.md with a MyST executable code cell wired into the book's _toc.yml; NumPy and Matplotlib deps are already in requirements.txt.

buildHints.whenToUse: Scientific documentation, course notes, research reports, or any project that publishes executable notebooks as a navigable multi-page website. Jupyter Book renders MyST Markdown and .ipynb files via Sphinx; outputs include static HTML and optionally LaTeX/PDF.
firstSteps: Install deps: `pip install -r requirements.txt` (installs jupyter-book, numpy, matplotlib).
Build the book: `jupyter-book build .` — HTML lands in `_build/html/`.
Preview locally: `python -m http.server --directory _build/html 8098` then open http://localhost:8098.
Validate the scaffold: `node validate-jupyter-book.mjs` — prints 'jupyter-book starter ok' when all required files are present.
Add more content: create `.md` or `.ipynb` files under `content/`, then list them as chapters in `_toc.yml`.
gotchas: `execute_notebooks: auto` in `_config.yml` runs code cells at build time — if NumPy or Matplotlib are missing from `requirements.txt` the build fails with a kernel error. Keep pip deps in sync with imports.
The `_toc.yml` `root:` field must be a file path without extension; it points to `content/intro`, not `content/intro.md`.
`{{headline}}` and `{{author}}` in `_config.yml` are template placeholders substituted at compose time — do not hard-code values there.
Jupyter Book caches notebook outputs in `_build/`; delete that directory when switching Python environments or after adding new packages to avoid stale kernel state.
The validator (`validate-jupyter-book.mjs`) requires Node.js — it checks structure only, not Python execution. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt` separately before the full `jupyter-book build`.
architectureNotes: All navigable pages are listed in `_toc.yml`; `_config.yml` sets global metadata, Sphinx extensions, and HTML theme options.
MyST Markdown (`.md`) and Jupyter Notebooks (`.ipynb`) are first-class citizens — mix them freely in `content/`.
The `execute_notebooks: auto` policy only re-runs cells when source has changed (Jupyter Book caches results); for reproducibility pin all package versions in `requirements.txt`.
